question: Which wave oscillates parallel to the motion of the sound wave?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Longitudinal Wave.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Longitudinal waves, the particles of the medium** oscillate parallel to the direction of the wave**.
 
• Longitudinal waves r**equire a medium(solid, liquid, or gas)** to propagate.
 
• The speed of the wave** depends upon the properties of the medium** such as density and elasticity.
 
• Common examples of Longitudinal waves are **sound waves in air, Seismic-P waves, and waves in springs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In Transverse wave, the particle displacement is in the** perpendicular direction** of the wave.
 
• Transverse wave features **Crests(highest point) **and** Troughs(lowest point).** The distance between Crests and troughs is called **Wavelength.**
 
• Tramsverse waves **cannot travel in gaseous medium.**
 
• Electromagnetic waves consist of Oscillating Electric and Magnetic fields.
 
• In a vacuum, electromagnetic waves travel at the speed of light which is approx.** 299,792 km/s(or 3 x 10⁸ m/s)**
 
• **Radio waves have long wavelengths **and **Gamma rays have Short Wavelengths**.
 
• Mechanical waves require a medium to propagate which means they can't travel in a vacuum.
 
• Mechanical waves are of two types: **Longitudinal Waves and Transverse Wave**
 
• Sound waves travels **fastest in Steel.**
